transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
On the same day that A.I. giant Anthropic posted the biggest initial public offering
on record, four people were arrested for blocking an entrance to Anthropic San Francisco offices
from member station KQED in San Francisco, one Carlos Lara reports.
As Anthropic made its stock market debut, more than 100 protesters gathered outside
of the company's offices to raise alarms over the risks of rapidly advancing artificial
intelligence.
Among those arrested was stop A.I. co-founder Guido Reichstader.
"This corporation is not engaged in a lawful business.
They just issued an IPO in which their risk filing stated that their activity here poses
the risk of catastrophic or existential harm to humanity."
On its website, Anthropic says RSI could increase risks of humans losing control of A.I.
For NPR News, I'm Juan Carlos Lara in San Francisco.
"Anthropic rose sharply in its Wall Street debut yesterday, overtaking SpaceX as the
largest IPO in history, but confidence in A.I. failed to reignite after Wall Street
losses Thursday, stocks in Asia declined on anxiety about an A.I. bubble, and European
shares opened lower today."
U.S. envoy Jared Kushner says President Trump is open to NATO-style security guarantees
for a postwar Ukraine, and that he believes Russia is comfortable with that.
"He sent a very strong message to both of them on the desire for peace and would like
to engage both of them very aggressively to get there, and I'm not going to go into the
private discussions that he had, I'll let him disclose that when he's ready.
But I believe he also came away believing that peace is achievable, and we need to all
work together to try and achieve it."
Kushner speaking in Berlin Thursday at a meeting of European allies who have expressed concern
about President Trump's meeting in China with Russian leader Vladimir Putin pushing
to be included in U.S.-backed talks to end the war.
A district attorney in southern Wisconsin will not bring criminal charges against a
white Madison police officer who fatally shot a black man in late July from Wisconsin public
radio Sara Lear reports.
Officer Kiel Battinger Peterson fired a total of three shots at 38-year-old Cory Ruiz just
after Ruiz went to the ground during an attempted arrest.
Dane County's district attorney Ishmael Ozan concluded the officer's actions were reasonable
after Ruiz did not follow commands, was not subdued by Tasers, and pulled out a knife.
Federal rights attorney Ben Crump is representing the Ruiz family.
He says officers had other options.
"Let me say for the record, we don't believe any of the shots were justified."
Officers used Tasers on Ruiz, but investigators said the devices didn't work properly.
For NPR News, I'm Sara Lear in Madison.
This is NPR.
Kenya has chosen a group of American companies to develop a critical minerals deposit used
in defense, electronics, and AI, an effort supported by President Trump, as Michael Koloki
reports.
Kenya's government announced that American consortium Frontier Minerals has been selected
to develop the Mrema Hill Critical Minerals deposit located in the southeast of the country.
Mrema Hill has been identified by U.S. officials as a key target in the Trump administration's
push to expand U.S. access to critical minerals.
Kenyan authorities say that the American consortium will be required to engage with local communities
and obtain prospecting licenses before development can proceed.
They say preliminary assessments suggest the area contains rare earth minerals worth billions
of dollars.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Koloki in Nairobi.
With more than an hour, according to the AP, prison staffers struggled to find a suitable
new entry.

topics.text: Anthropic IPO sparks San Francisco protest; four arrested at company offices
Anthropic's Wall Street debut overtakes SpaceX as largest IPO; Asian and European stocks fall
Jared Kushner says Trump open to NATO-style security guarantees for postwar Ukraine
Dane County prosecutor declines charges against Madison officer who fatally shot Cory Ruiz
Kenya selects American consortium Frontier Minerals to develop Mrema Hill critical minerals deposit
AP reports prison staffers struggled over an hour to find a suitable new entry
